rules.statement: A non-notarial agreement to sell is invalid if it contravenes the provisions of section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance.
rules.supporting_quote: (1) The agreement to sell, being a non-notarial document it contravenes the provisions of section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance and is therefore invalid. (2) A notice to quit is a condition precedent to a successful action for ejectment. The absence of a repudiation of the contents considered together with the averments in the pleadings and the evidence of the plaintiff-respondent under oath are adequate to come to a finding that the plaintiff-respondent had a valid contract of tenancy with the defendant-appellant. (3) Standard of proof to establish the contract of tenancy is on a balance of probability. On a preponderance of evidence led at the trial, the trial court has come to a finding on a balance of probability that a contract of tenancy existed. 394 (4) When the defendant-appellant entered the premises as a tenant he is precluded from claiming the premises for himself
